newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-FIFTH SEED KORDA BOUNCED FROM AT&T CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FIFTH SEED KORDA BOUNCED FROM AT&T CHALLENGE.

text.p: Unseeded Swede Magnus Norman deprived the AT&T Challenge of its highest remaining seed for the second consecutive night when he bounced fifth-seeded Czech Petr Korda in straight sets on Friday.
The 81st-ranked Norman reached his third career semifinal with a 6-4 6-4 victory over Korda just a day after picking off fourth seed Andre Agassi.
The top three seeds -- Michael Chang, Jonas Bjorkman and Jim Courier -- were all upset earlier in the week.
Norman earned a semifinal clash with seventh-seeded Australian Jason Stoltenberg, who had to play just four games before taking his place in the final four.

Stoltenberg moved on when Fernando Meligeni retired trailing 1-3 in the first set. The unseeded Brazilian had sustained a hip injury in his previous match and was unable to compete effectively Friday.
The other semifinal pits eighth-seeded American Chris Woodruff against unseeded Marcelo Filippini of Uruguay.
Filippini, the lowest ranked player remaining in the field at 92, advanced easily with a 6-1 6-2 rout of Austria's Gilbert Schaller.
Woodruff posted a 6-1 4-6 6-3 victory over unseeded Australian Sandon Stalle.
Woodruff shot to a 4-0 lead in 11 minutes and dominated the first set. But Stolle recovered and pushed the American to three sets before falling.

Norman, who keeps a daily diary of his play which he consults for advice before each match, had lost to Korda in their only previous meeting earlier this year. He said he deviated from his usual routine prior to the rematch.
"I didn't read the diary this time because I remembered that other match and that I should have won it," Norman said.
Throwing in big serves when he needed them, Norman took the first set, then broke Korda in the first game of the second set when the fifth seed double-faulted.
Korda, ranked 28 and still working his way back to form after two injury-plagued years, evened the match by breaking back for 2-2.
But forehand errors cost him a break in the ninth game and Norman used two of his 12 aces to serve out the victory 6-4.
"I knew I had to be less passive and try to play high balls and go in. It was the same strategy as against Agassi," Norman said, referring to his upset of the newlywed Agassi.
Norman said he will use a mental trick to help him get through the semifinal.
"I'll try to go out and think this is a match I'm playing at home in Stockholm," he said.
